occurrence: Title of Trystan S. Goetze’s paper “AI Art is Theft: Labour, Extraction, and Exploitation” (arXiv, version 2; first posted January 2024), which argues that image generators involve labour theft from artists.

P1.reason: “Theft” states wrongdoing as settled. As a moral argument about consent and pay, it is a position people can debate; as a statement of fact, US courts have not established it, and one court found a specific training use fair.

P2.reason: Applies to all AI art. Reproduction of training images and text has been shown in targeted tests of selected works, not in all output; imitating a style alone is generally not protected.

W1.reason: No distinct additional problem; the issue is scored once above.

W2.reason: No human-like agency is attributed to AI.
